about:
Midian Electronics was founded in 1975 by Chuck Soulliard in Tucson, Arizona. The company began by specializing in after-market 2805/1500 Hz and 600/1500 Hz MTS pulse tone decoders, as well as SECODE SMART/IMTS/DTMF radio-telephone encoders-decoders with ANI. Its name derives from "Miniature Digital and Analog," reflecting the focus on compact electronic modules for land mobile radio.

Today Midian designs and manufactures a broad line of radio communication products, including tone signaling modules (DTMF, pulse tone, two-tone, five-tone), voice security devices such as voice scramblers and AES-128 bit encryption, tone remote desk sets, termination panels, two-way radio interoperability switches, remote control and monitoring systems, fleet management, telephone interconnects, paging and alarm products, and plug-in modules for OEM radios. The company also offers in-house custom electronic circuit design, PCB layout, and product development services. All products are designed and built at its Tucson facility and carry a three-year parts and labor warranty.

Midian's equipment serves public safety agencies (police, fire, ambulance), fleet operators (taxi, towing, fishing), government and military users, industrial and commercial businesses, and OEM radio manufacturers. Its interoperability solutions, for example, bridge LTE to VHF or connect Site Connect to P25 networks.

The company distinguishes itself by being the first to bring after-market MTS pulse tone decoders to market and by introducing the world's first voice scrambler small enough to fit inside a portable two-way radio. Midian states its mission is to continue providing innovative, after-market products that improve the safety and versatility of two-way radio networks.
